Charge.notes: Mt. Rose-side Chute through a gate; reported steepest of the Charge/Detonator/Fuse trio with a sharp pitch at the top, exits into Tailings. No specific cliff or rock info.
Charge.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; steepseeker.com (difficulty 52.3, highest at Rose); sierraavalanchecenter.org obs (Charge Chute)

Detonator.notes: Gated Chute in the Charge/Detonator/Fuse group, steep pitch at the top and runout to Tailings. No cliff info.
Detonator.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; snowbrains.com Chutes trip report

Fuse.notes: Gated Chute next to Detonator (signed gate entrance), steep top, runs out to Tailings. No cliff info.
Fuse.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; firsttracksonline 2017 Rose report

El Cap.notes: Signature Chute off the El Cap gate from Northwest: longest, steepest line (~40-50 deg sustained, 1,500+ ft). Rocks are used for airs in comps, but no mandatory cliff reported.
El Cap.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); skimag.com Chutes tip sheet; mountainyahoos.com Mt Rose; thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes

Saddle.notes: Off the El Cap gate: opens as a bowl, then funnels into a 40-deg chute that pinches to ~2 ski lengths (the pinch can be skirted). Drop-in described as feeling like going off a cliff.
Saddle.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes

Jackpot.notes: Gated Double Diamond chute from Northwest (Jackpot gate also accesses Cardiac Ridge). Long sustained pitch where a fall means a long tumble. No specific cliff info.
Jackpot.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); mountainyahoos.com; thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes

Yellow Jacket.notes: Gated Double Diamond chute, long and steep. The Dragon Lady variant off this gate is the tightest line in the Chutes, but the main run has no specific cliff info.
Yellow Jacket.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); mountainyahoos.com; skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; peakrankings.com Chutes tour

Nightmare.notes: Lowest gate on the east side, served by the Chuter lift; steeper double-black next to Miller Time. No specific info on cliffs or rocks.
Nightmare.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; yourtahoeguide.com/2019/03/mt-roses-hidden-chutes

Chaos.notes: Chute cut through the trees (2004, widened since) with glades on both sides, reached from the Nightmare gate; nicely spaced trees lower right. Not rock-lined.
Chaos.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes

Cardiac Ridge.notes: Ridge line off the Jackpot gate with a cornice entrance: about 10 ft of air to clear by mid-season, then 45+ deg below. Has a 'crux first move' at the top.
Cardiac Ridge.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); skimag.com Chutes tip sheet; skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes

Hornet's Nest.notes: Gated Double Diamond with a constricted throat. Venom, off this gate, has a small cliff band about halfway down (one of few in the Chutes) and tight trees at the bottom.
Hornet's Nest.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; peakrankings.com Chutes tour

Gold Run.notes: Black-diamond bump run on the Slide/Zephyr side; OSM also tags it moguls. No info on cliffs or trees.

Beehive.notes: Gated Chute about 30-35 deg, fairly wide open, short because it drops off the ridge into the flats. Reached via the Mine Train traverse. Mellowest of the Chutes.
Beehive.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; yourtahoeguide.com/2019/03/mt-roses-hidden-chutes; unofficialrose.com

Miller Time.notes: Gated Chute described as a single-diamond warm-up that holds untracked snow. No hazard info.

Cutthroat.notes: Western Chutes gate off Northwest; steep but wider below Cardiac Ridge. OSM puts it on Magic, but it is in the Chutes. No info on cliffs.
Cutthroat.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); skiing-blog.com/mt-rose-chutes; thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; peakrankings.com Chutes tour

Lowball.notes: Last and lowest western Chutes gate, suggested as an easier alternative to El Cap. No hazard info.
Lowball.source: skirose.com/chutes (gated, expert-only, 40-55 deg, avalanche control); thetahoeweekly.com/2016/09/16-chutes-one-day-takes; skimag.com

Six Gun.notes: Northwest side; one of a trio of 'zipper-line bumpers' with Waterfall and Greg's Gamble (2001 report).

Waterfall.notes: Northwest side bump run, part of the Waterfall/Six-Gun/Greg's Gamble trio (2001 report).

Northwest Passage.notes: Popular Northwest run, groomed for high-speed cruising (2001 report). No hazard info.

Greg's Gamble.notes: Northwest bump run (trio with Six Gun and Waterfall). Steep, well-spaced trees lie between it and Ramsey's but are not the run itself.

Silver Dollar.notes: Wide-open terrain in East Bowl (2001 report). No hazard info.

Big Bonanza.notes: Groomed blue on the Slide/Zephyr side per OSM. No hazard info.

Washoe Zephyr.notes: Black-diamond bump run on the Slide/Zephyr side; bumps soften in morning sun.

Wild Card.notes: Slide side; OSM tags grooming=backcountry (likely ungroomed). No hazard info.

Bruce's.notes: Groomed run on the Slide/Zephyr side per OSM. No hazard info.

Lone Tree.notes: Galena lift area (Mt. Rose side). No info.

Mineshaft.notes: Black-diamond mogul run on the Lakeview side, shown as an example of Rose's mogul runs.

Ramsey's.notes: Groomed per OSM. Steep glades with sharp hidden rocks sit off the catwalk at upper Ramsey's, next to the run (2001 report).

Comstock Glade.notes: Named glade on the Slide/Winters Creek side, where glades are short, widely spaced trees with rock formations.

Little Red Glade.notes: Named glade near the bottom of the Chutes and Winters Creek side; low-angle tree run.

Express.notes: Groomed cruiser off Northwest (2001 report). No hazard info.

Playground.notes: Western side of the Chutes, off the Cutthroat gate. Low average grade, so likely a mellow apron. No hazard info.

Tailings.notes: Runout bowl where Charge, Detonator and Fuse exit, with low average grade. Gate status for Tailings itself is unknown. No hazard info.
